title: Opinionated Harnesses and Local Memory for Claude Code
summary: Riccardo Pirruccio shows how hooks and a local memory plugin make Claude Code agents more useful.

chapters.title: Why He Forked It for Ollama
Manufacturing and the Toyota LangGraph Talk
Q&A: Memory, Worker and the Local Model

learn: He traces the shift from prompt engineering to context engineering to today's harness engineering: a plug-in ecosystem of hooks, skills and tools around an agent (from a post by Viv).
claude-mem stores observations from your sessions in SQLite, injects context from earlier sessions at session start, and uses Chroma for vector search through an MCP; five hooks capture the session.

His fork runs the observation step on local Ollama on his RTX 4090 with a 7B model, so the session notes come from a local model instead of a hosted one; he credits the original project for the hooks, Chroma and compression.
A slide on fast-shipping AI tools and weak security, including the Moltbook API key exposure, makes the case for opinionated choices.
Takeaways: stay narrow and deep, make opinionated decisions, keep context local, and know the limits. He cites a Toyota LangGraph factory talk and NVIDIA's Voyager paper.
